title: pre-commit hook blocks commits on pre-existing PHPCS warnings
body:
## Problem

`.githooks/pre-commit` runs `vendor/bin/phpcs --colors "$FILE"` and treats any non-zero exit as failure. PHPCS exits 1 when a file has **warnings only**. Any edit to a file with pre-existing warnings is therefore blocked, even when the change adds no errors.

Example: `inc/models/class-base-model.php` has 6 pre-existing warnings (`PSR2.Classes.PropertyDeclaration.Underscore` on `$_original`, `$_mappings`, `$_mocked`; `Squiz.PHP.CommentedOutCode.Found` at about lines 732/737; `PSR2.Methods.MethodDeclaration.Underscore` on `_get_original`) and 0 errors. Committing #2004 failed with "Could not fully fix", and PHPCBF reported "No fixable errors were found".

## Fix

- File: `.githooks/pre-commit` (the `phpcs` calls at about lines 42, 60 and 75).
- Make the pass/fail checks ignore warnings, e.g. `vendor/bin/phpcs -n` or `--runtime-set ignore_warnings_on_exit 1`. Still show warnings for information if needed.

## Verification

- Stage a whitespace-only change to `inc/models/class-base-model.php` and run `git commit`. The hook passes, and PHPStan still runs.
- Stage a real PHPCS error (e.g. a non-Yoda comparison in `inc/`). The hook still blocks the commit.

### Files Scope

- `.githooks/pre-commit`

title: Secondary networks never get Ultimate Multisite tables created or upgraded
body:
## Problem

Ultimate Multisite only creates and upgrades its tables on the **main network**. On any other network in the same database it queries `wp_wu_{N}_*` tables but never creates them, and existing secondary-network tables never receive schema upgrades.

- `inc/database/engine/class-table.php`: `is_upgradeable()` returns false unless `is_main_network()`. BerlinDB's `maybe_upgrade()` (on `admin_init`) is the only automatic install/upgrade path, so it never runs on other networks. This has been the case since the initial commit.
- The only other path is `Core_Installer::_install_database_tables()` (setup wizard), which calls `$table->install()` directly.
- Multinetwork's cloner only creates unsuffixed `wp_wu_*` tables in tenant databases. Nothing creates `wp_wu_{N}_*` for networks in the same database.
- Tables with `$upgrades` (9 classes, e.g. `2.13.2`, `2.17.4`) are never upgraded on secondary networks.

### Reproduction

On current `main`, create network 3 (`wu_create_network()`) and mark setup finished. `Table_Loader` registers `wp_wu_3_customers`, but `is_upgradeable()` is false and `exists()` is false, and `wu_get_customers()` fails with `Table '…wu_3_customers' doesn't exist`.

## Fix

1. `Engine\Table::is_upgradeable()`: allow the main site of any network (`is_main_site()`).
2. On secondary networks, run each table's `maybe_upgrade()` on the first request (front end included), gated by one per-network option holding the tables' schema signature, so it runs once per schema change. Per-network version keys already exist (`wpdb_wu_{N}_{table}_version`, stored on the main network).

### Files

- `inc/database/engine/class-table.php`
- `inc/loaders/class-table-loader.php`
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/Database/Engine/Table_Test.php`

## Verification

- A new secondary network gets all plugin tables on its first request, and model queries have no DB errors.
- A secondary-network table with an older recorded version runs its pending upgrade.
- The main network behaves as before. Later requests don't re-run the check (a single option read).

title: Secondary networks: sunrise queries unregistered scoped tables, and wu_{N}_* tables are never created
body:
## Problem

On a multi-network install, Ultimate Multisite queries network-scoped tables (`{base_prefix}wu_{network_id}_*`) on secondary networks, but two paths leave those tables unusable:

1. **Sunrise domain mapping queries tables that were never registered.** `Sunrise::load_domain_mapping()` (`inc/class-sunrise.php:191-205`) starts `Domain_Mapping` on every network. On a network where Ultimate Multisite returns before `setup_tables()` (`inc/class-wp-ultimo.php`, the `Requirements::met() === false || Requirements::run_setup() === false` early return; `run_setup()` reads the per-network `wu_setup_finished` option), no `Table` object is built for that network. The domain `Query` still applies the network prefix (`Network_Prefix::update_prefix_with_network_id()`, `inc/database/engine/traits/trait-network-prefix.php:20-25`), so it reads `$wpdb->wu_{N}_domain_mappings`. That property is unset, which gives an empty table name:

   ```
   Table '<db>.wu_5_d' doesn't exist for query SELECT  wu_5_d.id FROM  wu_5_d WHERE wu_5_d.blog_id = 323 AND wu_5_d.domain != ...
   ```

   Note the double space: the table name is empty and only the alias `wu_5_d` remains. Production logged about 170 of these in 7 hours on one template network.

2. **Secondary-network tables are never created.** `Table::is_upgradeable()` (`inc/database/engine/class-table.php:50-57`) returns false unless the request is on the main network and main site, so `maybe_upgrade()` never installs `wp_wu_{N}_*`. A network ends up with none of these tables, or with only the subset some one-off path created. One network had customers/memberships/payments but no `posts`, `postmeta`, `webhooks`, `passkey_credentials`, `webauthn_challenges`, `email_otp_attempts` or `sso_nonces`. Addon tables that extend the core `Table` (e.g. metered-plans' `metered_usage`) inherit the same gap. A missing `posts` table also means a network has no system emails (`payment_received_*`, `site_published_*`, …).

## Expected

- Every secondary network that Ultimate Multisite serves has its full set of scoped tables, created idempotently when the network is first used or created, and on upgrade.
- Domain mapping at sunrise never builds a query against an unregistered table. Either register the network's tables (e.g. build the needed `Table` objects in `Sunrise::load_domain_mapping()` before `Domain_Mapping` runs), or fall back to the main network's tables when Ultimate Multisite is not set up on the current network.
- Default system emails get created for a network once its `posts` table exists.

## Workaround applied on one install (not a fix)

Ran in each affected network's `--url` context:
- `$t->install()` for every `Table_Loader::get_instance()->get_tables()` entry, plus `Metered_Usage_Table`, where `exists()` was false.
- `Email_Manager::get_instance()->create_all_system_emails()`.
- For the template network, set the `wu_setup_finished` network option so Ultimate Multisite completes loading and registers its tables.

Note: `Table::exists()` caches its result, so in the same process it still reported false right after a successful `install()`. A fresh process or `information_schema` showed the tables were present.

## Files to modify

- `inc/class-sunrise.php` (`load_domain_mapping`)
- `inc/database/engine/class-table.php` (`is_upgradeable`, and possibly the `exists()` cache)
- `inc/installers/class-core-installer.php` (network-scoped install)
- `inc/loaders/class-table-loader.php`
- `inc/managers/class-email-manager.php` (`create_all_system_emails` on new networks)

## Verification

On a multi-network test install:
1. Create a secondary network without running the setup wizard and request one of its mapped domains. There should be no `FROM  wu_N_` (empty table) errors.
2. Every `get_tables()` entry should `exists()` for that network after creation or upgrade.
3. `wu_get_emails()` should return the default system emails on that network.


### Files Scope

- `inc/class-sunrise.php`
- `inc/database/engine/class-table.php`
- `inc/installers/class-core-installer.php`
- `inc/loaders/class-table-loader.php`
- `inc/managers/class-email-manager.php`
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/Database/Engine/Table_Test.php`
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/Managers/Email_Manager_Test.php`

title: perf: lazy-load the top My Sites toolbar and defer initial site-list hydration
body:
## What

Lazy-load the **top WordPress My Sites toolbar dropdown beside My Networks** so an unopened menu does not enumerate and hydrate the full site list or construct every site's management links. This is not the bottom-right Toolbox/Jumper UI.

Keep current-site navigation and an explicit full My Sites administration link immediately available. Fetch bounded, paginated results only when the menu is opened or explicitly requested, preserving the existing site visibility rules, permissions and SSO/magic links.

## Why / measured evidence

Read-only authenticated local Users-request profiling, with the My Networks lazy-loading change already served:

| Region | Typical local elapsed | SQL queries | Blog-context events |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Initial Ultimate Multisite site-list preparation | 0.166–0.204s | 113 | 58 |
| WordPress My Sites submenu construction | 0.120–0.130s | 22 | 60 |
| Combined initial preparation plus menu | 0.2867s median across 3 runs | 135 | 118 |

Events count both switches and restores, not 118 distinct sites. Later site-list calls were already largely request-cached and added no SQL. The bottom Toolbox setup/render cost about 4ms and no additional SQL on the same request; do not optimize that unrelated UI for this issue.

These are inclusive instrumented CLI request-attribution measurements, not production HTTP savings. One additional run was substantially slower with identical operation counts, so do not promise a fixed latency reduction. Persistent Redis was disabled locally. Verify with controlled HTTP runs after implementing.

## Root cause and verified files

- `inc/managers/class-site-manager.php:1158-1277`, `hide_customer_sites_from_super_admin_list()`: builds up to 40 site objects plus the main site. Reads of `$site->blogname` and `$site->siteurl` hydrate WordPress site details and activate downstream blog-switch hooks.
- `inc/managers/class-site-manager.php:1280-1362`, `is_frontend_my_sites_toolbar_request()` and `get_current_site_for_frontend_my_sites_toolbar()`: existing **opt-in, frontend-only, direct-toolbar-initialization** optimization is a reference pattern. It intentionally excludes admin/AJAX/REST/CLI and protects nested `get_active_blog_for_user()` calls. Do not simply remove those guards.
- `inc/sso/class-admin-bar-magic-links.php`: existing My Sites node rewriting must remain effective for lazily loaded links.
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/Managers/Site_Manager_Test.php`: existing toolbar context, filtering, user scope and archived/spam/deleted tests.
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/SSO/Admin_Bar_Magic_Links_Test.php`: existing magic-link coverage.
- `DESIGN.md`: record the changed interaction and fallback behavior.

Reference the WordPress core `WP_Admin_Bar::initialize()` / `get_blogs_of_user()` preparation path and `wp_admin_bar_my_sites_menu()` separately. Deferring just the submenu callback leaves the initial 113-query hydration cost intact. Core lives in the WordPress installation, not in this plugin repository; inspect its installed implementation rather than guessing repository paths.

Use the existing site manager for the authenticated endpoint and add `assets/js/my-sites-toolbar.js` for the native toolbar controller, following existing asset conventions. If investigation requires a different write surface, record and validate the amended scope before editing. Related implementation reference: Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite-multinetwork#63, which lazy-loads My Networks with pagination, nonce checks, retry and keyboard/touch support. It is a reference, not an implementation dependency or an assumption that the PR has merged.

### Files Scope

- `inc/managers/class-site-manager.php`
- `inc/sso/class-admin-bar-magic-links.php`
- NEW: `assets/js/my-sites-toolbar.js`
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/Managers/Site_Manager_Test.php`
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/SSO/Admin_Bar_Magic_Links_Test.php`
- `DESIGN.md`

## Bounded implementation contract

1. Restrict the lightweight initial site-list behavior to the direct toolbar initialization context; do not globally change `get_blogs_of_user()` for profile links, dashboards, admin screens, REST clients or application code.
2. Preserve existing allowed-site filtering and current-user context. The lazy endpoint must be authenticated, nonce-protected and server-authorized. Do not expose unrelated sites, globally cache capability decisions, or weaken authorization.
3. Return at most 10–20 sites per fetch, with deterministic ordering and explicit pagination. Do not preload the complete list in script localization or hidden HTML.
4. Preserve network/site-specific URLs, customer-owned-site visibility semantics, existing `get_blogs_of_user` filters and magic-link/SSO behavior. Restore any switched context in a `finally` block.
5. Retain current-site and full-list navigation without JavaScript. Support hover, keyboard focus and touch; provide loading, empty and explicit retry states, no duplicate in-flight requests, and no focus theft on hover.
6. Cover admin and frontend toolbar paths. Do not modify WordPress core or unrelated installed plugins. Do not enable the existing frontend optimization setting globally as a substitute for this implementation.

## Acceptance / verification

- [ ] Unopened toolbar does not perform full managed-site enumeration/detail hydration or per-site submenu construction.
- [ ] Opening the menu fetches only a bounded page; load-more results are disjoint and full-list access remains available.
- [ ] Verify current-site navigation and generated links under both subdomain and subdirectory multisite, mapped domains and secondary networks where available.
- [ ] Preserve permission denial, customer/non-super-admin behavior, site-state filtering and magic-link behavior. No cross-user/site information disclosure.
- [ ] Keyboard activation, Escape/focus return, touch layout, failed-request retry and JavaScript-disabled fallback work in the real rendered product.
- [ ] Existing affected Site_Manager and Admin_Bar_Magic_Links suites pass, with only narrow new boundary coverage; no new test runner/harness is needed.
- [ ] Run scoped PHPCS/ESLint/PHPStan and inspect standard PHP/browser errors.
- [ ] Repeat authenticated HTTP before/after benchmarks with identical user pagination, revisions and cache configuration. Record actual HTTP time separately from CLI attribution; count both scalar and bulk cache-key reads and actual backend calls separately.
- [ ] Do not claim the 0.5-second target is reached without runtime evidence. Do not merge or deploy as part of worker implementation without the normal authorized lifecycle.

Rollback: revert the isolated lazy-toolbar change to restore the existing eager menu; no persistent data migration is required.

## Pre-flight and routing

- [x] Memory recall: My Sites toolbar/cache performance query returned no relevant stored lessons; current-session runtime evidence is supplied above.
- [x] Discovery: scoped recent-commit, merged-PR, open-PR and claimed-issue searches returned no matching work. Additional open searches for My Sites performance/toolbar returned no matches.
- [x] File references: the five implementation/test/design paths above were verified as tracked; line numbers reflect the inspected revision and must be rechecked at worker pickup.
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — existing authorization patterns within a defined toolbar-only boundary; not a mechanical exact-edit task.
- [x] Seeded draft PR: skipped; preserve the measured finding without anchoring a worker to an unverified patch.

Leaf implementation task. Dispatch: #auto-dispatch. Create a focused implementation PR referencing this issue; no release or deployment is requested.

title: fix(sites): grid bulk Delete removes real sites matching pending sites' membership IDs
body:
## Bug: bulk "Delete" in the Sites grid view deletes real sites whose blog ID equals a pending site's membership ID

**Severity:** critical, silent data loss (site tables and uploads are dropped).

### What happens

In **Network Admin → Ultimate Multisite → Sites**, the default **grid view** of the "All Sites" tab renders pending sites with a selection checkbox whose value is the **membership ID**:

- `views/base/sites/grid-item.php` (pending branch): `name="bulk-delete[]" value="<?php echo esc_attr($item->get_membership_id()); ?>"`

The bulk action submitted from that tab is the regular `delete` action for model `site` (`Site_List_Table::get_bulk_actions()` only switches to `delete-pending` when `type=pending`). `Base_List_Table::process_bulk_action()` then runs `wu_get_site($id)->delete()` for every submitted ID, so each membership ID is treated as a **blog ID** and `wp_delete_site()` removes an unrelated live site.

The list view already guards against this (`Site_List_Table::column_cb()` omits pending checkboxes outside the dedicated Pending view), but the grid template does not.

### Reproduction

1. Have a pending site owned by membership `N`, and an unrelated published site with blog ID `N`.
2. Open Sites (grid view, All Sites), tick "Select Site" on the pending card, choose bulk **Delete**, confirm.
3. Blog `N` is deleted; the pending site remains.

Observed in production: selecting leftover pending test signups deleted three unrelated customer sites whose blog IDs matched the pending sites' membership IDs.

### Fix

- `views/base/sites/grid-item.php`: mirror `column_cb()` and render the pending checkbox only in the dedicated Pending view (`type=pending`), where the bulk action is `delete-pending` and membership IDs are the expected values.
- Defence in depth in `Base_List_Table::process_bulk_action()` / site bulk delete: refuse to delete when the request comes from a view that lists pending items with membership-ID values (or validate that submitted IDs are real blog IDs shown in that view).

### Verification

- Grid view, All Sites: pending cards show no bulk checkbox; bulk Delete of regular sites still works.
- Pending view: bulk delete removes only the pending-site records (`delete-pending`), no `wp_blogs` rows change.
- `vendor/bin/phpunit` for the site list / pending-site deletion tests; `vendor/bin/phpcs` on changed files.

Arabic-script invoice content currently selects `xbriyaz`, which `Invoice::get_rtl_fontdata()` maps to the bundled Amiri fonts with OpenType Layout enabled. The maintainer review reproduced the exact `Mpdf\Exception\FontException: GPOS Lookup Type 5, Format 3 not supported (ttfontsuni.php)` with Arabic text. It traced the failure to unsupported contextual-substitution tables in the bundled font. Treat this as evidence to reproduce against the current default branch and installed mPDF, not as permission to assume dependency versions or copy reviewer code verbatim.

The same uncaught PDF failure affects invoice viewing/downloading and the `phpmailer_init` attachment callback. A PDF failure must not abort a payment email.

### Implementation

1. Reproduce Arabic PDF generation through the real `WP_Ultimo\Invoices\Invoice` class using Arabic text such as `فاتورة مرحبا بالعالم`; include regular and bold content. Verify the installed mPDF version, exported classes, retained font filenames and packaging before changing mappings.
2. Replace the unsupported Amiri mapping with the retained DejaVu Sans Condensed regular/bold fonts, keeping `xbriyaz` automatic language selection, OpenType shaping (`useOTL`) and kashida settings. The review verified this alternative renders connected RTL Arabic and needs no new dependency or font download. Preserve the existing available_unifonts registration pattern. Check whether the `amiri` alias has compatibility consumers and retain a safe alias if necessary. Remove the obsolete custom font directory method/call and update associated docblocks.
3. Remove the four obsolete Amiri font binaries only after confirming no remaining source, packaging, or release reference requires them. Do not broaden this into changes for Hebrew, Thai or Devanagari fonts.
4. In `Email_Manager::attach_invoice_pdf()`, contain invoice construction/rendering exceptions, log a useful sanitized error using the existing `wu_log_add()` pattern, and allow the email to send without the failed PDF attachment. Preserve the subject guard and unrelated attachment behavior; never log invoice content, customer billing data or secrets.
5. In `Payment_Manager::invoice_viewer()`, preserve all existing payment ownership/access checks. Contain invoice creation/rendering failures and return a translated, escaped user-facing error rather than an uncaught exception or raw exception details. Do not send a corrupt/partial PDF as a successful response.

### Files Scope

- `inc/invoices/class-invoice.php`
- `inc/managers/class-email-manager.php`
- `inc/managers/class-payment-manager.php`
- `assets/fonts/amiri/Amiri-Regular.ttf`

- `assets/fonts/amiri/Amiri-BoldItalic.ttf`
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/Invoices/Invoice_Test.php`

Reference patterns: `Invoice::get_missing_fontdata()` already remaps stripped fonts to retained fonts; `Invoice_Test::test_pdf_with_special_characters()` exercises the real Invoice class and checks a generated PDF. The payment manager already uses `wu_log_add()` and `LogLevel::ERROR` for contained exceptions.

### Verification and acceptance

- Add one focused Arabic regression case to the existing Invoice_Test suite; use real PDF generation, no new harness or test-only interfaces. Assert a nonempty valid PDF with Arabic text and bold content without a FontException. Preserve Latin invoice generation.
- Run `vendor/bin/phpunit --filter Invoice_Test` and repository-required focused gates using its existing local test environment. Run `vendor/bin/phpcs inc/invoices/class-invoice.php inc/managers/class-email-manager.php inc/managers/class-payment-manager.php tests/WP_Ultimo/Invoices/Invoice_Test.php` and PHP syntax checks on modified PHP files.
- Render the actual Arabic PDF to an image using existing tooling when available and independently inspect connected glyphs and right-to-left ordering. Record evidence; do not claim visual verification from a PDF header alone.
- Exercise existing email and viewer paths or existing tests to confirm PDF failure no longer aborts mail, viewer failures are controlled, and unauthorized users still cannot access invoices. Report inaccessible integration prerequisites honestly; do not add testing infrastructure to bypass them.
- Recheck obsolete font references, package-size impact and `git diff --check`. Follow repository guidance for any required documentation/design update.
- Open the implementation PR with `Resolves #<this implementation issue>` and `Ref #1925`; include verification evidence. The original locked report remains for maintainer closure after verifying delivery. Do not publish a release, update the host lockfile, deploy, or touch production as part of this task.

This is a trusted maintainer-owned code brief, not a request for more advisory review. It is authorized for normal automated implementation, verification and PR workflow. ## Problem

After #2013, a secondary network's first request runs `Table::maybe_install_network_table()` (`inc/database/engine/class-table.php`). For an **existing** `wu_{N}_*` table whose BerlinDB version key is missing, BerlinDB stamps the table as current **without running its upgrade callbacks**:

- `needs_upgrade()` reads `get_network_option(get_main_network_id(), "wpdb_wu_{N}_{table}_version")` (`vendor/berlindb/core/src/Database/Table.php:910-913`). Missing → `false` → upgrade needed.
- The table exists, so `upgrade()` runs. `get_pending_upgrades()` returns `[]` when `db_version` is empty (`Table.php:718`), so `upgrade()` calls `set_db_version()` with the current version and returns (`Table.php:679-684`).
- Then the table is recorded in `wu_network_table_versions` and never checked again until its version changes.

Two real-world states reach this path:

1. **Versions recorded under the secondary network's own `sitemeta`** (`site_id = N`) instead of the main network. Observed on a production install: one network had 38 `wpdb_wu_{N}_*_version` keys only under its own `site_id`, none under the main network. Another had 13 keys under both. Whatever wrote them (likely an install or upgrade run with `get_main_network_id()` resolving to the secondary network, e.g. the multinetwork add-on or a one-off installer) is not identified yet.
2. **Tables with no version key anywhere.** Observed: 4 tables on one secondary network (`forms`, `formmeta`, and two support-ticket add-on tables).

**Current impact: none observed.** Every recorded version on that install equals the current code version, and the one version-less core table with an upgrade callback (`wu_{N}_forms`) already has the post-`2.0.1-revision.20230601` schema (nullable `date_created`/`date_modified`). The risk is latent: a schema bump that ships before these networks are stamped, or an older network with pre-upgrade tables, would skip upgrades silently.

## Proposed fix

In `Table::maybe_install_network_table()`, before calling `upgrade()` on an existing table with no main-network version:

1. **Adopt a network-local version.** If `get_network_option($network_id, $this->db_version_key)` has a value, copy it to the main network key (BerlinDB's source of truth) so `get_pending_upgrades()` runs the right callbacks. Optionally delete the stray network-local key after the upgrade succeeds.
2. **No version anywhere.** Decide between:
   - (a) treat it as the oldest baseline and run all upgrade callbacks (current core callbacks are idempotent `ALTER ... MODIFY COLUMN`, but add-on callbacks such as metered-plans `add_cost_value_column` must be checked for idempotency), or
   - (b) keep BerlinDB's stamp-current behaviour, but log it (`wu_log_add`) so the drift is visible.

   Recommendation: (1) plus (2b) unless all registered callbacks are verified idempotent.

## Files

- `inc/database/engine/class-table.php`: `maybe_install_network_table()`.
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/Database/Engine/Table_Test.php`: follow the pattern of `test_secondary_network_table_is_upgraded_on_first_request`, but record the old version under `site_id = N` instead of the main network and assert that the upgrade ran.
- Unknown: the code path that wrote versions under the secondary network's `site_id`. Search `set_db_version`, `get_main_network_id` filters, and the multinetwork add-on's installer to identify it.

## Verification

- A secondary table whose old version exists only under its own network's `sitemeta` runs its pending upgrade callbacks on first request (column nullability changes, as in the existing upgrade test).
- A version-less existing table is handled per the chosen option (upgrades run, or a log entry is written).
- The main network and already-stamped secondary networks are unchanged (one cached option read).

Ref #2013, Ref #2012
